summary: Cambodia issues a 30-day tourist eVisa online (30 USD) and a 30 USD visa on arrival to most nationalities, while ASEAN neighbors enter visa-free. Travellers arriving by air must complete the free Cambodia e-Arrival card within 7 days before arrival.

declarations.name: Cambodia e-Arrival Card (CeA)
declarations.text: Cambodia's e-Arrival card combines the immigration, customs and health declarations in one free online form (web or Cambodia e-Arrival app). Travellers arriving by air at Phnom Penh (Techo), Siem Reap Angkor or Sihanoukville must submit it within 7 days before arrival; the portal says any traveller can submit it.

notes: Canada's travel advice says the Cambodia e-Arrival forms cover immigration, customs and health, and must be completed within 7 days of your scheduled arrival.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says US dollars are widely used alongside the riel, but only newer, undamaged notes are accepted — notes with the slightest tear are refused. Credit cards are not widely accepted outside major cities, and ATMs are plentiful in Phnom Penh, Siem Reap and Sihanoukville but fewer in smaller towns.

safety.text: The UK advises against all but essential travel within 20 km of the land border with Thailand, where landmines and unexploded ordnance also remain; Canada and Australia advise against all travel within 50 km of it, and the land crossings with Thailand are closed. Australia advises a high degree of caution in the rest of the country. Watch for bag-snatching by thieves on motorbikes, and be alert to scams, including organized-crime compounds advertised as easy, well-paid jobs. Stick to marked paths in remote areas.

idp.text: Cambodia is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

tips.text: Apply for the eVisa only on the official site, evisa.gov.kh.
Bring US dollar notes in good condition: Canada's travel advice says only newer, undamaged notes are accepted, and Australia's Smartraveller says sellers may refuse dirty, torn or high-value notes.
The Cambodia e-Arrival card is free. If you arrive by air, complete it within 7 days before you arrive, at arrival.gov.kh or in the official Cambodia e-Arrival app.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Cambodia?
faq.answer: Yes. US passport holders need a tourist visa: either the eVisa (30 USD, applied for at evisa.gov.kh) or a visa on arrival (30 USD) at airports and major land borders; the land crossings with Thailand are currently closed. Both allow a 30-day stay, extendable once by 30 days.

faq.question: Is the Cambodia eVisa better than the visa on arrival?
faq.answer: They cost the same (30 USD online or at the border) and both give 30 days. The eVisa is accepted only at the Techo (Phnom Penh), Siem Reap Angkor and Sihanoukville airports and the Bavet and Trapeang Kriel land crossings — Cham Yeam and Poipet on the Thai border are temporarily closed to eVisa entry — so check your entry point first.

faq.question: What is the Cambodia e-Arrival card?
faq.answer: The Cambodia e-Arrival (CeA) is a free online form combining immigration, customs and health declarations, submitted within 7 days before arrival at arrival.gov.kh or via the Cambodia e-Arrival app. It is required if you arrive by air at Phnom Penh, Siem Reap or Sihanoukville.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Cambodia?
faq.answer: A tourist (T) visa can be extended once by 30 days at the immigration department or through agents. For longer stays, enter on an ordinary (E-class) visa instead. It can be extended in-country for 1, 3, 6 or 12 months.

faq.question: Which nationalities enter Cambodia visa-free?
faq.answer: Citizens of ASEAN countries enter visa-free: 30 days for Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Laos, Singapore and the Philippines, 14 days for Thailand, Myanmar and Brunei. Maldivian (30 days) and Seychellois (15 days) ordinary passports are also exempt. Nearly everyone else needs the eVisa or a visa on arrival.
